findings.title: TRWLightLock.WriteLock returns while readers are still inside the critical section
findings.explanation: TryWriteLock computes f := Flags and not 1, which clears only the writer bit and keeps the reader count in the upper bits. It then CAS-es Flags from f to f+1. With two readers holding the lock, Flags = 4, f = 4, the (Flags = f) test passes and the CAS 4 -> 5 succeeds, so TryWriteLock returns true while those readers are still running. WriteLock is now just 'if not TryWriteLock then WriteLockSpin', and WriteLockSpin is 'repeat SpinAndWait until TryWriteLock' - neither waits for the reader count to reach zero. The write bit only blocks readers that arrive afterwards, because ReadLock CAS-es from the same masked f and fails once bit 0 is set. Existing readers are never drained. A writer therefore mutates or frees data another thread is dereferencing. The prior code took the write bit the same way but then ran 'while Flags <> 1 do spin := SpinAndWait(spin)' to wait for every reader to leave; that second loop is gone.

evidence.why: f keeps the reader count, so the CAS f -> f+1 succeeds with readers present: Flags=4 gives f=4, (Flags = f) is true, CAS 4->5 succeeds.
The only exit condition is TryWriteLock, which does not require the reader count to be zero. No drain loop remains, so WriteLock returns with readers still inside.
A concrete writer that frees the object readers are dereferencing under the same TRWLightLock (fRouterSafe).

reachability.reachable_from: TRestServer.Uri - every HTTP/REST request - racing TRestServer.ResetRoutes, reached from TRestServer.SetOptions/ServiceMethodRegister and TServiceContainerServer.AddServiceInternal/SetPublishSignature

findings.refuted_by: Ruled out: (1) 'not 1' masks bit 0 only and LockedExc is a plain InterlockedCompareExchange, so the CAS from f succeeds at any reader count - nothing tests the reader bits; (2) WriteUnLock is LockedDec(Flags, 1), decrementing only the write bit, so it is built to coexist with readers; (3) ReadLock/TryReadLock CAS from the same masked f, blocking only readers that arrive after the bit is set; (4) no {$ifdef} guards these routines; (5) no external serialisation - ResetRoutes relies on fRouterSafe alone while Uri holds only a ReadLock. Upstream 7dd5c8c6d fixes exactly this, citing #557.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the two-phase acquisition in WriteLockSpin: after CAS-ing the write bit on top of the reader count, spin with 'while Flags <> 1 do spin := SpinAndWait(spin)' until all readers have left. TryWriteLock must stay all-or-nothing, i.e. CAS from 0 to 1 only, so a caller that gets true really is exclusive - that is what upstream 7dd5c8c6d does.

findings.title: TRWLightLock.TryWriteLock grants an exclusive write lock while readers still hold it
findings.explanation: TryWriteLock computes f := Flags and not 1, which clears only the writer bit and keeps the reader count that lives in bits 1..31/63. It then tests Flags = f, which is true whenever no writer holds the lock no matter how many readers do, and CAS-es f -> f+1. With Flags = 2 (one reader inside its critical section) f = 2, the guard passes, LockedExc(Flags, 3, 2) succeeds, and TryWriteLock returns true; WriteLock returns to its caller while that reader is still running. Nothing drains the readers afterwards: WriteLockSpin is now just 'repeat SpinAndWait until TryWriteLock', and the second loop that used to wait for all readers once the writer bit was taken is gone. New readers and a second writer are still correctly blocked once bit 0 is set (ReadLock's CAS from f fails, and the second TryWriteLock sees Flags <> f), so the breakage is precisely the writer/existing-reader overlap: the writer mutates data that concurrent readers are still dereferencing.

evidence.why: f keeps the reader bits, so 'Flags = f' only asserts that bit 0 (the writer bit) is clear. Any non-zero reader count still satisfies it and the CAS succeeds.
The blocking path adds no reader drain of its own: it accepts whatever TryWriteLock accepts, so WriteLock inherits the same non-exclusive acquisition.
Confirms LockedExc is a plain CAS returning true on success, so TryWriteLock really does report an acquired write lock in the f<>0 case.
The reader side of the race: every HTTP request dereferences fRouter under a TRWLightLock ReadLock, i.e. with Flags >= 2.

reachability.reachable_from: TRestServer.Uri (every HTTP request) racing TRestServer.ResetRoutes, reached from the public ServiceMethodRegister / TServiceFactoryServer.SetOptions paths

findings.refuted_by: Looked for what would make it safe and found nothing. The old reader-drain 'while Flags <> 1 do spin := SpinAndWait(spin)' is deleted with no replacement; ReadLockSpin, ReadUnLock and IsLocked do not drain either. grep over src/ shows a single TRWLightLock.TryWriteLock / WriteLockSpin implementation, so no asm or per-platform .inc variant escapes it. ReadLock and a second TryWriteLock are correctly rejected once bit 0 is set, which narrows the defect to the existing-reader overlap but does not remove it.
findings.suggested_fix: Make the write bit only obtainable on a fully free lock, i.e. 'result := LockedExc(Flags, {to=}1, {from=}0)', or keep the f+1 CAS inside WriteLockSpin and restore the second loop that waits until Flags = 1 before returning - but then TryWriteLock must not report success while reader bits remain set.

findings.title: TRWLightLock.WriteLock now returns while ReadLocks are still held
findings.explanation: TryWriteLock computes f := Flags and not 1, which clears only the writer bit and keeps the reader counter in bits 1..31/63. It then requires (Flags = f), i.e. only that no writer holds the lock, and CASes Flags from f to f + 1. With N readers inside their critical section Flags = 2N and f = 2N, so the test passes, the CAS succeeds, and the writer bit is set while those N readers are still reading. WriteLock is now nothing but 'if not TryWriteLock then WriteLockSpin', and WriteLockSpin only retries TryWriteLock: the second loop that used to drain the readers after taking the writer bit ('while Flags <> 1 do spin := SpinAndWait(spin);') was deleted by this change, and the old from=0 comperand that made the fast path require an idle lock is gone too. So a WriteLock call returns to its caller with readers active, and the lock no longer provides the exclusion its callers rely on.

evidence.why: f keeps the reader counter, so the comperand is the current reader count, not 0: the CAS succeeds and sets the writer bit while readers hold the lock.

The slow path is now only a retry of TryWriteLock. The 'while Flags <> 1' loop that waited for all readers to leave after acquiring the writer bit no longer exists, so nothing waits for readers anywhere.
Confirms LockedExc returns true whenever Target equalled Comperand, so a non-zero (readers-present) comperand is an accepted acquisition, not a rejection.
A writer that proceeds while readers are active here frees fRouter under a thread that is dereferencing it, turning the exclusion defect into a use-after-free.

reachability.reachable_from: TRestServer.Uri, the main REST processing method (every HTTP request), as the reader; TRestServer.ResetRoutes, reached at runtime from SOA registration in mormot.soa.server, as the writer

findings.refuted_by: No asm override exists: 'git grep RWLightLock' over *.inc at this sha returns nothing and no other unit implements these methods, so the Pascal bodies run on every platform. LockedExc in mormot.core.base.pas returns true iff Target = Comperand, so a reader-count comperand is accepted. ReadLock/TryReadLock do block new readers while bit 0 is set, but nothing makes an in-flight reader leave. WriteUnLock (LockedDec(Flags, 1)) only clears the writer bit. WriteLockSpin's whole body has no reader-drain loop left.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the two-stage acquisition in WriteLockSpin: after the CAS that sets the writer bit, spin until Flags = 1 so all readers have left; and keep the fast path in WriteLock/TryWriteLock CASing from 0 so it only succeeds on a fully idle lock.

findings.title: TRWLightLock.WriteLock no longer waits for in-flight readers, breaking read/write exclusion
findings.explanation: TryWriteLock computes f := Flags and not 1, which keeps the reader counter in the upper bits, then CAS-es Flags from f to f+1: it succeeds as soon as bit 0 (the writer bit) is clear, whatever the reader count is. WriteLockSpin now only spins until that same TryWriteLock succeeds; the previous second loop 'while Flags <> 1' that waited for all readers to drain is gone, as is the old inline fast path LockedExc32(Flags, 1, 0) that only succeeded from an idle Flags=0. WriteLock therefore returns while readers are still inside their critical section. New readers are still blocked and writers still exclude each other, so what is lost is exactly writer-vs-reader exclusion. TRestServer.Uri holds fRouterSafe.ReadLock across fRouter.Lookup(ctxt) on every request, while ResetRoutes takes fRouterSafe.WriteLock and does FreeAndNil(fRouter): a router reset now frees the object under a request thread that is dereferencing it. ComputeRoutes republishes fRouter under live readers the same way.

evidence.why: f keeps the reader bits (only bit 0 is masked off), so the CAS from f to f+1 succeeds with readers still counted in Flags: the writer bit is taken without exclusion against active readers.
The whole body is the acquire loop; there is no remaining loop waiting for Flags to drop to 1, i.e. no drain of the existing readers anywhere in the new implementation.
The write side frees fRouter as soon as WriteLock returns, relying entirely on WriteLock having drained the readers.
The read side of the same lock in TRestServer.Uri dereferences fRouter inside the read critical section, on every HTTP request.

reachability.reachable_from: TRestServer.Uri (HTTP request entry point) racing any caller of the public TRestServer.ResetRoutes, e.g. the Options setter TRestServer.SetOptions or TServiceContainerServer.AddServiceInternal.

findings.refuted_by: WriteLockSpin's whole body is the TryWriteLock loop; TRWLightLock has one implementation, no per-platform .inc variant; LockedExc is a plain pointer-sized CAS, so 'Flags = f' plus the CAS excludes another writer, not readers; WriteUnLock's LockedDec(Flags, 1) is consistent with readers counted concurrently, confirming the intent rather than fixing it. ResetRoutes' 'if fRouter = nil then exit' does not help (it is the non-nil path that frees) and Uri has no second guard around fRouter.Lookup. The prior code did drain: 'while Flags <> 1 do // second loop to wait for all readers'.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the reader drain: keep TryWriteLock strictly optimistic (CAS from 0 to 1, i.e. no reader and no writer), and in WriteLockSpin keep the two loops -- first CAS the writer bit in from 'Flags and not 1', then spin 'while Flags <> 1' until every reader has left before returning.

findings.title: TRWLightLock.WriteLock returns while read locks are still held
findings.explanation: TRWLightLock packs the state in one word: bit 0 is the write flag, bits 1..n are the reader count (ReadLock atomically adds 2). The reviewed TryWriteLock computes f := Flags and not 1, checks only that bit 0 is clear (Flags = f), then CAS-es Flags from f to f + 1 -- so with one reader present (Flags = 2) it takes f = 2, sees Flags = f, swaps 2 -> 3 and returns true. WriteLock is now just 'if not TryWriteLock then WriteLockSpin', and WriteLockSpin spins only 'until TryWriteLock': the second loop that used to wait for the reader count to drain ('while Flags <> 1') is gone. The write lock is therefore granted while readers are inside the critical section. Two consequences. Same thread: a ReadLock followed by WriteLock no longer deadlocks as the header documents, it silently succeeds. Different threads: a writer mutates or frees data a reader is walking. Only the plain Flags = 0 case is still handled correctly.

evidence.why: TryWriteLock only tests bit 0, keeps the reader bits in f, and CAS-es to f + 1; WriteLockSpin loops on TryWriteLock alone, with no wait for readers.
ReadLock keeps the reader count in the bits above bit 0, so Flags = 2 means one active reader -- exactly the value TryWriteLock accepts.
The header still promises the old contract -- a nested WriteLock/TryWriteLock after a ReadLock 'would deadlock' -- which the code above no longer honours.
A real writer: ResetRoutes frees fRouter under the write lock it now shares with concurrent readers.

reachability.reachable_from: TRestServer.Uri (every HTTP request) reads fRouter under fRouterSafe.ReadLock while public TRestServer.ResetRoutes -- from SetOptions/SetRoutingClass/ServiceMethodRegister -- frees it under WriteLock

findings.refuted_by: Read the whole TRWLightLock body at this sha (Init, ReadLock, TryReadLock, ReadUnLock, ReadLockSpin, TryWriteLock, WriteLock, WriteUnLock, WriteLockSpin, IsLocked): no reader drain anywhere, and no {$ifdef} around TryWriteLock, so no platform escapes it. LockedExc in mormot.core.base.pas is a plain PtrUInt CAS, not a stronger primitive. WriteUnLock is LockedDec(Flags, 1), clearing only bit 0 -- itself built on readers coexisting with the write flag. fRouterSafe has no second guard: Uri dereferences fRouter with only ReadLock.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the two-stage acquisition: after winning bit 0, spin until the reader bits are clear (the previous 'while Flags <> 1 do spin := SpinAndWait(spin)' loop), and keep TryWriteLock a straight CAS from 0 to 1 so it fails whenever any reader holds the lock.
